correctness.rationale: The group has eight elements and acts faithfully. Invariant quadrics (A,B,C) are basepoint free by direct quartic substitution; f*O(1)=2H gives degree 16, so the quotient map has degree 2. The exact identity Z^2-A(A-4B)Q=-16WU^2d^2 was independently computed by full symbolic expansion and verified from the embedded package. The three reduced factors form two distinct lines and a smooth conic with determinant 128; pairwise restrictions give five transverse crossings and no triple point. As Z gives the nontrivial quadratic extension, normality identifies the double-plane hypersurface with X/G. At each crossing the normal double plane has A1 singularity, elsewhere it is smooth. Double-plane adjunction yields -K ample and K^2=2; the crepant resolution has five exceptional (-2)-curves. Scope characteristic zero and geometric.

originality.rationale: The exact source paper gives W, the order-eight coordinate permutation group and invariant lattices for individual symmetries, but not the explicit global quotient. Fallucca--Pignatelli already has two-line/conic branch five-node del Pezzo examples, but their source coverings and subgroup quotient constructions are different; numerical basket alone is NOT claimed novel. Targeted source/alias/parameter searches, six published-finding corpus searches and published comparisons gave no result covering the precise K3/D8 invariant map and double-plane equation. Remaining historical risk is acknowledged; novelty is best-knowledge, not an exhaustive uniqueness certificate.
residual_risks: A classical Fermat quartic quotient or invariant-ring calculation may be unindexed or inaccessible, particularly because the source quartic is geometrically Fermat after a linear change of coordinates.
Published five-nodal degree-two del Pezzo types are not unique: originality concerns the exact identified quotient and equation, not that surface type.
Uludağ 2005 was compared using accessible classification passages rather than a page-by-page full-text examination of every historical example.

value.rationale: The full quotient of the explicit K3 surface under its natural maximal coordinate-permutation subgroup is a canonical object motivated by the source paper’s use of nondiagonal symmetries. The constructed invariant map provides a complete intrinsic quotient equation, all five singularities, the anticanonical degree, and the crepant resolution type. This geometric quotient classification is not a parameter relabeling or generic inference from five-node tables; it allows direct comparison between the whole nonabelian symmetry and individual K3 involutions in the original work.
